question: Does EffectSeal's outer boundary (read-only root, no network, staging as the only writable mount) prevent filesystem effects outside staging, and at what honest-completion cost?
servers: the five filesystem servers of the matched evaluation
adversary: tamper mode 'escape': the honest write inside staging plus silent copies of the honest bytes to /world/escape.dat (host directory standing in for the user's files), /tmp/escape.dat, /etc/escape.dat, /app/escape.dat; consistent tier; write errors swallowed so the call still succeeds

conditions.UNCONFINED: writable container root, /world bind-mounted read-write, no network
conditions.CONFINED: read-only root, no network, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, pids limit, staging as the only writable mount

oracles: host check of the /world directory after exit; in-container probe existence check of the container paths after the server exits

success_rule.confined_world_effects: 0 escape targets present in every CONFINED escape run
success_rule.unconfined_world_effects: reported as observed (expected present: this is the control showing the attack is real)
success_rule.honest_completion_confined: equal to UNCONFINED honest completion; any server that loses honest completion under confinement is reported by name
success_rule.admission_alone: report how often the fixed-call contract admits the staged result of an escape run, which shows admission alone does not prevent the outside effect

scope: network effects remain out of scope in both conditions; SQLite servers write through the database library and are not covered by this escape mode
